039c1f98041e81d8939fead5f8ffa1f20ab2db6a.prompt: Build a pomodoro timer app with a big circular countdown, work/break cycles, and a satisfying chime when a session ends.
039c1f98041e81d8939fead5f8ffa1f20ab2db6a.plan:
- Single index.html, inline CSS+JS
- 25min work / 5min break, configurable
- SVG ring countdown animation
- WebAudio for the chime, no external assets
039c1f98041e81d8939fead5f8ffa1f20ab2db6a.summary:
The pomodoro app is built — a single self-contained `index.html` with no external assets, ready to preview in a browser.

What it includes:

- **Big circular countdown**: an SVG ring that drains smoothly as time passes, with the time, phase label, and pomodoro count in the center. The ring and accent color shift from red (work) to green (break).
- **Work/break cycles**: 25-minute work and 5-minute break defaults, plus a 15-minute long break after every 4 pomodoros. All four values are configurable via the settings panel, and sessions auto-advance so cycles flow continuously.
- **Satisfying chime via WebAudio**: a soft bell with an octave shimmer partial — a rising C-E-G arpeggio when work ends, a gentler two-note descent when a break ends. No audio files needed; the AudioContext is unlocked on the first Start click so browsers allow playback.
- **Extras**: Start/Pause/Resume, Skip, and Reset buttons, spacebar to toggle, the remaining time mirrored in the tab title, and a timestamp-based timer (rather than counting intervals) so it stays accurate even when the browser throttles background tabs.

10ea87e33a1af8ee129ee28a3805e29ab55d835a.prompt: add a theme button that allows the user to pick from a few different theme colors.
10ea87e33a1af8ee129ee28a3805e29ab55d835a.summary:
The theme picker is in. Here's what I added to `index.html`:

- **Theme button** — a pill button fixed in the top-right corner with a dot showing the current accent color. Clicking it opens a dropdown menu; clicking outside or pressing Escape closes it.
- **Six themes** — Tokyo Night (the original, default), Ocean, Forest, Rose, Ember, and a Light theme. Each menu option shows a three-dot swatch preview (background, work accent, break accent), and the active theme is outlined.
- **CSS variable overrides** — each theme is a `body[data-theme="..."]` block that overrides the existing `--bg`, `--panel`, `--text`, `--muted`, `--work`, and `--break` variables, so the timer ring, buttons, inputs, and work/break mode colors all follow the theme automatically. I also converted the one hardcoded input border color into a `--border` variable so it themes correctly too.
- **Persistence** — the choice is saved to `localStorage` (wrapped in try/catch for sandboxed previews) and restored on load.

No timer logic was touched, so the work/break cycling, chime, and keyboard shortcut all behave exactly as before.

801b90b597ff357daca5635d041a3bba4adabaae.prompt: Add a settings panel to tweak work/break durations, and show total pomodoros completed today (persist in localStorage).
801b90b597ff357daca5635d041a3bba4adabaae.plan:
- gear icon toggles a small settings panel
- inputs for work/break minutes, validated 1-120
- daily counter resets at midnight
801b90b597ff357daca5635d041a3bba4adabaae.summary:
The settings panel and daily counter are in place. Everything is in `index.html`, evolving the existing app:

**Gear-toggled settings panel** — the always-visible duration inputs moved into a floating panel in the top-left, opened by a gear button (inline SVG icon that rotates when open). It closes on outside click or Escape, and the settings panel and theme menu close each other so only one is open at a time.

**Validation 1–120** — work, break, and long-break inputs all accept 1–120 minutes. On change, out-of-range or non-numeric values are clamped back into range, a brief "Minutes must be between 1 and 120." error shows in the panel, and the valid values are persisted to localStorage (`pomodoro-settings`) so durations survive reloads — saved values are restored and re-clamped on load.

**Daily pomodoro counter** — a 🍅 chip under the controls shows "N pomodoros completed today." It increments only when a work session runs to completion (skipping doesn't count), persists to localStorage as `{date, count}` under `pomodoro-daily`, and resets at midnight: stale dates are discarded on load, and a 30-second interval catches the rollover while the app is left open overnight.

The existing timer behavior — timestamp-based ticking, chimes, themes, keyboard shortcuts, and live duration adjustments mid-session — is unchanged.

130d7206c7535710dec0dd2203849156f64e57ae.prompt: Add an optional soft ticking sound during the last 10 seconds of any session (toggle in settings, default off).
130d7206c7535710dec0dd2203849156f64e57ae.summary:
Done. The pomodoro timer now has an optional soft ticking sound for the last 10 seconds of any session, all within the existing `index.html`.

What I added:

- **Settings toggle**: a new "Sound" section in the settings panel with a "Tick last 10 sec" checkbox, styled to match the panel (18px, accent-colored). It defaults to off and is persisted in the same `pomodoro-settings` localStorage entry as the duration settings, so the choice survives reloads.
- **The tick itself**: a short WebAudio triangle-wave blip (~1050 Hz, 70 ms decay, low gain) — quiet and soft, generated with no audio assets, consistent with how the existing end-of-session chime works.
- **Trigger logic**: inside the timer's `tick()` function, whenever the displayed second changes while running and 1–10 seconds remain, the tick plays — so it fires exactly once per second during the final countdown of work, break, and long-break sessions alike. Enabling the checkbox also calls `ensureAudio()` so the AudioContext is unlocked by that user gesture.

With the toggle off (the default), behavior is unchanged.

ec1f3a6dce13f28d7aeac516ac4453fad0719107.prompt: Reskin the pomodoro as CAPYDORO, a capybara onsen timer: work sessions are Focus, breaks are Soak, long breaks are Deep Soak. A tiny capybara beside the ring sinks lower into a hot spring as a session progresses (and relaxes fully during soaks, with steam wisps). The daily 🍅 counter becomes yuzu — "N yuzu earned today". Warm onsen palette as the default theme. Everything else stays: ring countdown, chime, ticking option, settings, keyboard shortcuts, theme picker, localStorage.
ec1f3a6dce13f28d7aeac516ac4453fad0719107.summary:
CAPYDORO is in place — I reworked `index.html` (the whole app is that one file) to apply the reskin while leaving the timer machinery untouched.

What changed:

- **Naming**: The app is now titled CAPYDORO, with phases renamed Focus / Soak / Deep Soak everywhere — the ring label, session counter ("Focus #N"), browser tab title, and the settings fields ("Focus (min)", "Soak (min)", "Deep soak (min)", "Focus / deep soak").
- **Capybara onsen scene**: A small SVG hot spring sits beside the ring (wrapping below it on narrow screens). The capybara starts chin-height in the water and sinks gradually as a Focus session progresses, driven by a `--sink` CSS variable updated on each render and clipped to the pool so it never pokes out the bottom. During Soak/Deep Soak it settles fully in (deeper for Deep Soak), closes its eyes, gets a blush, bobs gently, and three animated steam wisps rise off the water. Two yuzu float in the spring for the classic yuzu-yu touch.
- **Yuzu counter**: The 🍅 pill is now a small yuzu SVG icon with "N yuzu earned today", still persisted under the same localStorage key with midnight rollover.
- **Onsen theme**: A warm palette (dark roasted-brown background, persimmon for Focus, yuzu gold for Soak, teal spring water) is now the `:root` default and the first option in the theme picker. Tokyo Night moved to an explicit `data-theme="tokyo"` block, and all six previous themes remain selectable; the light theme gets a darker steam color so wisps stay visible.

Everything else — ring countdown, chime, last-10-seconds ticking option, settings validation and persistence, Space shortcut, Escape to close panels, and all existing localStorage keys — carries over unchanged, so returning users keep their saved durations, daily count, and theme choice.
